props.title: Lady Dragon

sections.content: **Lady Dragon** (1992) sits at a fascinating intersection of female-led martial arts films that emerged in the early 1990s. Starring Cynthia Rothrock, who blazed a trail for Western women in Hong Kong action cinema with films like Yes, Madam (1985) and Righting Wrongs (1986), this Indonesia-shot revenge thriller follows familiar beats but stands out for its raw intensity. Like **Above the Law** (1988) and **Angel of Fury** (1991), it capitalizes on the martial arts boom of the era while giving its female lead agency and physical prowess rarely seen in American action films of the time.

sections.content: The film's influence can be traced through later female-driven martial arts films like **Wing Chun** (1994) and **China O'Brien** (1990). Rothrock's portrayal of Kathy Galagher showcases legitimate martial arts credentials - she holds black belts in multiple disciplines - lending authenticity to the fight sequences. Director David Worth, who also helmed **Kickboxer** (1989), brings a straightforward approach that emphasizes practical stunts and extended combat scenes over narrative complexity. SUBHEAD: The Rise of Female Action Stars in the 1990s

**Lady Dragon** (1992) emerged during a crucial period when female action stars were gaining prominence. While Hong Kong had embraced powerful women warriors through performers like Angela Mao in **When Taekwondo Strikes** (1973) and Michelle Yeoh in **Police Story 3: Supercop** (1992), Western cinema was just catching up. Rothrock's success helped pave the way for later stars like Milla Jovovich in **The Fifth Element** (1997) and Michelle Rodriguez in **Girlfight** (2000).
